steps.observation: You have 30 seconds. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here’s a quick rundown in under 30 sec:

1. Sugar backbone  
   • DNA has deoxyribose (one less –OH group)  
   • RNA has ribose (one extra –OH)

2. Strands  
   • DNA is usually double-stranded (double helix)  
   • RNA is usually single-stranded

3. Bases  
   • DNA: A, G, C, T (thymine)  
   • RNA: A, G, C, U (uracil replaces thymine)

4. Function & location  
   • DNA stores hereditary information, stays in the nucleus (in eukaryotes)  
   • RNA carries and helps execute genetic instructions (mRNA, tRNA, rRNA), moves to the cytoplasm for protein synthesis
